Topic1.Title: Open Comment (Public Participation)
Topic1.Summary: Residents spoke during open comment, with many advocating to keep the pool and gym at the South Boulder Rec Center, including youth swimmers and petition signers. Other speakers raised concerns about the voice and sight dog tag program, ambulance provider practices, power resilience and microgrids, the lack of housing for families, and international issues including Gaza. Staff said they would follow up on the dog tag program, the ambulance concerns, and the energy resilience suggestions. Council noted that no decision has been made on the South Boulder Rec Center, that $2 million was budgeted in 2025, and that study sessions on the long-term financial strategy and rec centers are scheduled for March 12 and April 9.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic2.Summary: Council considered consent agenda items 3A and 3B, which were moved and seconded. Following a roll call vote, both items were approved unanimously.

Topic3.Title: Public Hearing: Annexation and Land Use Change for the Hogan-Pancost Property
Topic3.Summary: Council held a public hearing on the petition to annex approximately 24.04 acres, including city-owned land at 5399 Kowani Drive and 5697 South Boulder Road and a portion of 55th Street right-of-way. Staff and the Parks and Recreation Department explained that the city purchased the property in 2019 for flood mitigation and parks purposes and that no development plans are part of this review. The Planning Board unanimously recommended approval, and the proposal includes Public zoning on most of the site and RL-2 zoning for the right-of-way. Council unanimously adopted Resolution 1370, Ordinance 8734, and the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan land use map change from low-density residential to Parks, Urban and Other for the western 19 acres.

Topic4.Title: Public Hearing: Concept Plan Review for 4880 and 4898 Pearl Street (Boulder Storage Site)
Topic4.Summary: Council reviewed a concept plan for redeveloping the Boulder Storage site with four residential buildings containing 281 apartments and an 85,000-square-foot storage building, which requires a concept review but no formal action. Staff found the residential use likely inconsistent with the general industrial designation and the East Boulder Subcommunity Plan, and explained that the proposed phasing relies on a contiguity interpretation that could make other nearby industrial parcels eligible for housing. The applicant argued that the site is underused, that the project would generate significant tax revenue and a $13 million cash-in-lieu contribution, and that Goose Creek should count as open space for contiguity. Council members expressed concern about losing industrial land and setting a precedent, encouraged a revised concept that preserves industrial and live-work uses and better engages the multi-use path, and asked staff to clarify the contiguity rules.
